title: infra check and init take any NOERROR reply as the authoritative server's answer and never read its AA flag -- a tunnel that answers port 53 itself read as 37 ttl drifts, and a cache that matches the profile reads as held
body:
FOUND 2026-10-14 by prodinfra-cc on hv's machine, read at about 07:00Z by its account, against the vendored runtime 0.1.10 (bb1cd07c, manifest 7c39d91c), and sent to vc by message. Filed on hv's word to vc in session, "Yes, file." (vc's date -u read 08:07:17Z). Filed under the demo hold: nothing is built until hv lifts it.

THE SETUP. A commercial VPN's full WireGuard tunnel carried every port-53 query, to any address, and the tunnel answered each one itself.

THE EVIDENCE, prodinfra-cc's:
- `dig @198.51.100.1 +time=3 +tries=1 example.com A` came back NOERROR with 2 answers, flags qr rd ra ad. 198.51.100.1 is in TEST-NET-2 (RFC 5737), where no DNS server is.
- `dig @ns1.hover.com +norecurse MX geodica.com` came back REFUSED, flags qr ra, SERVER 216.40.47.26, and the same over TCP. An authoritative server answers for its own zone with AA set, and does not set RA. prodinfra-cc adds that every answer ns1.hover.com seemed to give carried RA, and that its REFUSED replies to +norecurse carried no AA.
- `bin/devbin infra check` against its geodica profile reported "37 assertion(s) held, 37 drift, 0 NOT MEASURED". Every MX, SPF and DMARC ttl read 30 against the 300 declared.
- Over DNS-over-HTTPS (dns.google) the same records read with identical content at ttl 300.
- Runs against its matthewsinclair and ficton profiles minutes earlier, through the same tunnel, held their ttls. So whether the false drift shows depends on the tunnel's cache, and nothing in the output says either way.

WHAT HAPPENS, read by vc at main e50be2ac, whose lib/ is 99dd3106's:
- infra_dns_read (lib/infra.dns:263) asks through _idns_ask (lib/infra.dns:130): `dig +noall +comments +answer +time=3 +tries=2 @<ns> <name> <type>`. It sends no +norecurse, so whatever answers at that address can resolve the question itself and answer from its cache.
- It judges a reply by its header status alone (lib/infra.dns:266-269): NOERROR or NXDOMAIN is read as the authoritative server's answer. The reply already carries the flags line, and nothing reads it, so an answer without AA is taken as authoritative. Checked on this machine's dig 9.10.6: `dig +noall +comments +answer` prints `;; flags: qr rd ra ad; ...` straight after the `->>HEADER<<-` line the status is read from.
- check compares the rows as configured values. _ic_ttl_check (lib/infra.check:200-209) says so, "the CONFIGURED ttl, because the reads are authoritative", and reports "ttl is 30, profile declares 300" as drift for MX, SPF and DMARC (:124, :140, :191) and for a wildcard (:451). The DKIM read (:291) and the wildcard reads (:423, :457) go through the same reader. A cache's ttl is the REMAINING ttl, which is what lib/infra.dns:21-33 says the authoritative read exists to avoid.
- init reads MX, SPF and DMARC through the same readers (lib/infra.init:157, :165, :174) and votes the ttl target from what they return (:159-198, :256-263), so a profile init proposes under interception carries the tunnel's remaining ttl as its target.
- The authority read (lib/infra.dns:205) asks the machine's resolver for NS by design, so its reply carries no AA and is not this issue's. Nameservers are an input, not a measurement (lib/infra.dns:35-38).

WHY IT MATTERS. infra's contract (lib/infra.dns:5-19) is that it reads each domain's records from that domain's own nameservers and keeps COULD NOT MEASURE apart from MEASURED. Here every read measured a different server and was reported as measured. That gave false drift today, and it gives a false held wherever the cache matches the profile, including a real change at the authority hidden behind a stale cache. The matthewsinclair and ficton runs went through the same tunnel, so their held verdicts measured the tunnel, not the domains. It is 0142's class one step later: there the machine's resolver stood in for the authority on the NS read; here whatever answers port 53 stands in for it on every record read.

NO ARM DRIVES IT. The fake dig prints a header line with a status and no flags line (tests/lib/infra_fakes.bash:118), so no arm can serve an answer without AA, and its strict argv check (:20, :89) refuses any argv lib/infra.dns does not send today.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO (vc's reading; cc builds it and vc reviews it):
- Read the flags line of every record reply and require AA. A NOERROR or NXDOMAIN reply without AA is NOT MEASURED for its facet, naming the server asked and what came back (eg "answered without AA: flags qr rd ra"). A referral carries no AA either, and today it reads as a measured absence (rc 0, no rows); the fix decides what a referral is and says so.
- Ask with +norecurse, so a recursive server at the address does not resolve the question on devbin's behalf. A REFUSED is already NOT MEASURED (lib/infra.dns:268).
- Name the cause once per run when a run meets an answer without AA. prodinfra-cc's probe does that: one short query to an address where no DNS server is (198.51.100.1, TEST-NET-2) proves interception when anything answers, and proves nothing when nothing does. Sent only after an answer without AA, it costs a run that is not intercepted nothing; sent before every run, it costs each such run its whole timeout.
- check and init say it in the same words, from one place, as they do 0142's sentence.
- Arms: the fake gains a flags line, aa by default, and a directive to withhold it. An answer without AA is NOT MEASURED in check and abstains in init, with the text asserted whole. A REFUSED to +norecurse stays NOT MEASURED. The existing arms keep their claims. Red first on main, green under BSD and GNU.
- Pages: lib/pages/infra.md, where it says what a measured read is and what COULD NOT MEASURE covers.

It ships in the next release, with everything open.

## Resolution

Landed at cccfd9ff on a green full suite (vc's, 2307 of 2307 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261014-0945). Ships in the next release.

- **A record is read without recursion and measured only on AA.** Every record read asks dig with +norecurse: MX, the SPF and `_dmarc` TXT, each DKIM record, the wildcard RRsets and the wildcard CNAME. infra_dns_read reads the flags line beside the status. A reply without AA is NOT MEASURED, whatever its status, and says what came back: `answered without AA: <status>, flags <flags>`, in check's row and in init's entry alike. A REFUSED stays NOT MEASURED, and when it carries no AA, as a real refusal does, it says so too. infra_dns_noaa is the one test of that line, so nothing else a failed read prints sends the probe or reaches a row. The authority read is unchanged: it asks the machine's resolver, with recursion, and reads no AA.
- **A referral is NOT MEASURED, never an absence.** It carries no AA, and it came back NOERROR with no record, so a DKIM name delegated away from the domain read as a HALF PAIR. devbin reads each name from the domain's own nameserver and follows no delegation, and the page now says so.
- **The cause is named once per run, from one place.** A run that met a reply without AA asks one question of 198.51.100.1, in TEST-NET-2, after every domain: example.com A, without recursion, on the run's budget. infra_dns_cause is the one wording, pure, as infra_dns_no_authority is for the authority read. When anything answers there, check prints the sentence as a `Cause:` line under COULD NOT MEASURE, not as a row, and init records it under `unreviewed:` as `interception`. Silence there names nothing. A dig that cannot ask the question is said in place of a cause, in dig's own words, rather than taken for silence.
  - It is asked at most once per run, however many replies lacked AA: check asks after every domain is read, and init after every domain is measured.
  - The trigger is any reply without AA, REFUSED included, where the issue named an answer without AA. Measured on hv's machine at 08:54Z on 2026-10-14, through the tunnel: asked with +norecurse, a.iana-servers.net and 198.51.100.1 both came back REFUSED, flags qr ra. With the fix the reported tunnel produces refusals rather than cached answers, so a trigger on NOERROR and NXDOMAIN alone would never name it.
  - The cost follows from that trigger. On a network that does not intercept, a lame or refusing nameserver, or a delegated name, now costs one probe timeout per run, up to DEVBIN_INFRA_DNS_TIMEOUT x DEVBIN_INFRA_DNS_TRIES seconds (6 by default). A run whose every reply carries AA pays nothing.
- **init abstains.** A record read without AA is `!unread`, so the domain abstains from that census and from the ttl vote, and a profile proposed through a cache takes no ttl from it.
- **The fake dig** prints the flags line dig prints: `qr aa` for a record read unless !FLAGS gives others, and `qr rd ra` from the resolver. It takes a record read only with +norecurse, and answers a question put to TEST-NET-2 only under !INTERCEPT, whose `noreply:<n>` makes dig unable to ask it. DIG_LEGACY=1 also accepts the pre-0193 record read, for a red-first run. probes_sent, which reads its log, lives beside it.
- **Red on main first**, under BSD and GNU with DIG_LEGACY=1: 9 of the 11 new arms, each at its own claim. Main reported ttl 30 as drift, held a matching cache at rc 0, read a referral as a HALF PAIR, sent no probe and named no cause, and proposed the cache's ttl as init's target. The other 2 hold the probe to runs that meet a reply without AA, and are green on main by design. The two claims critic-shell's round added are red on the first version too: it took a probe dig could not ask for silence, and init's entry gave no reason.

Declared:
- an interceptor that forges AA passes every check here, and the probe is never asked, since no reply lacks AA;
- the probe proves interception only of what reaches TEST-NET-2, so a path that intercepts only some addresses leaves its replies without AA unexplained, though every read still says what came back;
- the fake's flags line carries an ANSWER count that nothing reads.
